subcategory_description: Government benefits and payments for people who are not working or are raising a family.
label: Jobseeker Support, single, 25 or over, before tax (weekly)
context: The maximum weekly rate. The payment is reduced by the income of the person or their partner.

label: Jobseeker Support, single, 20 to 24, before tax (weekly)
context: The maximum weekly rate. The same rate applies to a single person aged 18 or 19 who is not living with their parents or caregivers.

label: Jobseeker Support, single, 18 to 19, living with parents, before tax (weekly)
context: The maximum weekly rate for a single person aged 18 or 19 living with their parents or caregivers.

label: Jobseeker Support, couple without children, before tax (weekly, each)
context: The maximum weekly rate for each partner. The couple's total is $717.50.

label: Jobseeker Support, sole parent, before tax (weekly)
context: The maximum weekly rate for a person with dependent children and no partner.

label: Weekly income limit, single, 25 or over
context: Before tax. A single person aged 25 or over must have a weekly income below this amount to get Jobseeker Support. The limits are higher for couples and sole parents and lower for people under 25.

label: Parents' combined income limit for 18- and 19-year-olds
context: Before tax. From 2 November 2026, an 18- or 19-year-old without dependent children must meet the Parental Assistance Test, which is passed if their parents' combined income is at or below this limit or they cannot reasonably rely on their parents for support.
